candidate.transition: branch one boundary variable over current quotient states, simplify, factor variable-disjoint components, discharge only locally certified query-irrelevant SAT components, then exact structural merge
candidate.closed_component_rule: only components containing no remaining boundary variable may be summarized or dropped
candidate.unresolved_rule: retain component exactly; never guess SAT/UNSAT

factor_law: SAT(C1 AND ... AND Cr) = AND_i SAT(Ci) for variable-disjoint CNF components
merge_law: structural-renaming merge allowed only after explicit bijection verification with all remaining boundary variables pinned
frozen_controls: STAR_VS_PATH_SELECTOR must collapse from 2^k structural classes to one query-state when each processed gadget closes as certified SAT 2-CNF
closed contradictory 2-SAT factor must propagate UNSAT
closed mixed-sign width-3 factor not covered by certified atom language must remain unresolved
remaining-boundary-connected factor must not be discharged early
random-small transform semantics must match independent exhaustive SAT reference

adversarial_family.name: CONNECTED_SELECTOR_BACKBONE
adversarial_family.purpose: test whether otherwise-easy factors stay coupled to future boundary variables so peak quotient width can still grow before final discharge
adversarial_family.allowed_interpretation: scoped limitation of this factor language only; not evidence for P!=NP

proof_obligations: every dropped component has a checkable polynomial-time SAT certificate from the frozen atom language
no candidate path enumerates all boundary assignments
state count and peak count are recorded before final query readout
finite family success does not imply asymptotic SAT-in-P
